I don't have any notes on Ezekiel 7 for you yet. I tried to fetch six commentary pages, but none of the text reached me. The fetch ran, then my script crashed because the results came back in a format it didn't expect. After that I wasn't allowed any more tool calls this turn, so I never read a page.

Your rules say I can only report what the pages actually say. Writing verse notes from memory would break that rule, so I've left them out completely rather than guess.

**Pages I tried to fetch (none of their content reached me):**
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-7/
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/7.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/ezekiel/7.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezekiel/7.htm
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel-7-commentary
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Ezekiel+7

**What I'd do next time:**
1. **Part 1 (traditional reading):** read the six pages above verse by verse. The likely points are the "end" in vv. 2–6, "the rod has budded" in vv. 10–11, buying and selling in vv. 12–13, gold becoming a stumbling block in v. 19, the profaned "treasured place" in v. 22, and "forge the chain" in v. 23.
2. **Part 2 (Protestant differences):** search each tradition's own sites on the verses where views tend to split. These are mainly whether God's judgment rules out pity (vv. 4, 9), what "know that I am the LORD" means (vv. 4, 9, 27), and how the chapter relates to the "Day of the LORD."
3. **Part 3 (other views):** check the NET Bible notes on the hard Hebrew words in vv. 10–11, any Bible Odyssey pages, and Catholic or Orthodox sites. I'd also see whether teachers on these sites use v. 19 ("their silver and gold cannot save them") against prosperity teaching.

Ask me to continue and I'll fetch these pages again and write the verse-by-verse notes with a URL for every point. I'll leave out anything I can't find a source for.
